w: “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!”
k: No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever.

w: “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
k: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

w: “Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him, and bring him.
k: Go your way into the village over against you: and as soon as ye be entered into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon never man sat; loose him, and bring him.

w: For most certainly I tell you, whoever may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening; he shall have whatever he says.
k: For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.

w: “Have faith in God.
k: Have faith in God.

w: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and immediately he will send him back here.”
k: And if any man say unto you, Why do ye this? say ye that the Lord hath need of him; and straightway he will send him hither.

w: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
k: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.

w: “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations?’
But you have made it a den of robbers!”
k: Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.

w: Therefore I tell you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.
k: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have

w: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
k: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

w: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”
k: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

w: “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
k: I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

w: For whoever is not against us is on our side.
k: For he that is not against us is on our part.

w: “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”
k: If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.

w: “The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”
k: The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.

w: Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.
k: And whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

w: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna,
into the fire that will never be quenched—
k: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

w: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”
k: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.

w: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.
k: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.

w: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
k: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

w: “What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”
k: What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?

w: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
k: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

w: “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.
k: Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.

w: “What are you asking them?”
k: What question ye with them?

w: “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”
k: O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.

w: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.
k: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

w: Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
k: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.

w: “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”
k: If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.

w: “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?
k: Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.

w: “Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”
k: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

w: “How long has it been since this has come to him?”
k: How long is it ago since this came unto him?

w: If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna
of fire,
k: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire:

w: “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”
k: Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

w: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna,
into the unquenchable fire,
k: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

w: “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
k: Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.

w: “This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting.”
k: This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.

w: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
k: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

w: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
k: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

w: that ‘seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’”
k: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.

w: “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
k: Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?

w: “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
k: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

w: “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,
k: Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:

w: “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
k: Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?

w: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
k: But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

w: “Peace! Be still!”
k: Peace, be still.

w: and as he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds
came and devoured it.
k: And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

w: The farmer sows the word.
k: The sower soweth the word.

w: Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,
k: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,

w: “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be given to you who hear.
k: Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.

w: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
k: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

w: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.
k: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.

w: yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
k: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

w: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes, and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
k: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

w: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
k: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

w: “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
k: Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?

w: “Is the lamp brought to be put under a basket
or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?
k: Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?

w: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
k: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

w: “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
k: So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;

w: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
k: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.

w: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow,
k: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:

w: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”
k: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

w: For there is nothing hidden, except that it should be made known; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.
k: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.

w: “Let’s go over to the other side.”
k: Let us pass over unto the other side.

w: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
k: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:

w: For whoever has, to him will more be given, and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”
k: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.

w: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
k: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

w: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.
k: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

w: For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
k: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

w: Others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
k: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

w: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
k: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter.

w: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
k: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,

w: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
k: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.

w: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.
k: And the gospel must first be published among all nations.

w: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand, or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
k: But when they shall lead you, and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost.

w: Most certainly I say to you, this generation
will not pass away until all these things happen.
k: Verily I say unto you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.

w: But you watch.
“Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
k: But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things.

w: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
k: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

w: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
k: Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death.

w: “It is like a man, traveling to another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
k: For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.

w: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
k: And let him that is on the housetop not go down into the house, neither enter therein, to take any thing out of his house:

w: “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
k: Take heed lest any man deceive you:

w: “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
k: Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

w: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
k: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.

w: lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping.
k: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

w: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
k: And let him that is in the field not turn back again for to take up his garment.

w: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
k: And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken.

w: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’
and will lead many astray.
k: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.

w: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
k: For in those days shall be affliction, such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created unto this time, neither shall be.

w: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
k: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

w: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
k: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

w: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
k: And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect’s sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.

w: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
k: So ye in like manner, when ye shall see these things come to pass, know that it is nigh, even at the doors.

w: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch.”
k: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.

w: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
k: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

w: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming, whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
k: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning:

w: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
k: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet.

w: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
k: And then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or, lo, he is there; believe him not:

w: For there will arise false christs and false prophets, and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
k: For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.

w: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
k: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When her branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is near:

w: But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
k: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

w: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
k: But woe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!

w: But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
k: But take heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye shall be beaten: and ye shall be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.

w: But when you see the abomination of desolation,
spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
k: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judaea flee to the mountains:

w: “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
k: Be not afraid, only believe.

w: “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
k: Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

w: “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”
k: Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.

w: “Who touched my clothes?”
k: Who touched my clothes?

w: “Talitha cumi!”
“Girl, I tell you, get up!”
k: Talitha cumi;Damsel,arise.

w: “What is your name?”
k: What is thy name?

w: “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
k: Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.

w: “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”
k: Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

w: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.”
k: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared.

w: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,
k: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

w: “For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.
k: For the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.

w: “Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
k: Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.

w: Whoever of you wants to become first among you, shall be bondservant of all.
k: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.

w: “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”
k: With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

w: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”
k: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

w: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
k: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

w: “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”
k: How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

w: “Go your way. Your faith has made you well.”
k: Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.

w: But many who are first will be last; and the last first.”
k: But many that are first shall be last; and the last first.

w: If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery.”
k: And if a woman shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.

w: “What do you want me to do for you?”
k: What would ye that I should do for you?

w: They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”
k: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

w: “Call him.”
“Children, how hard is it for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
k: Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

w: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.
k: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles:

w: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.
k: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.

w: “You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
k: Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.

w: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.
k: Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.

w: “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you shall be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with;
k: Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:

w: “What do you want me to do for you?”
k: What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?

w: “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,
k: Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel’s,

w: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
k: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

w: “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
k: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

w: and the two will become one flesh,
so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
k: And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.

w: “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
k: Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?

w: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.
k: But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:

w: For the Son of Man also came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
k: For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

w: “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
k: One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

w: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’”
k: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

w: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.
k: But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.

w: “What did Moses command you?”
k: What did Moses command you?

w: “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.”
k: Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while:

w: “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
k: A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

w: “Cheer up! It is I!
Don’t be afraid.”
k: Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.

w: “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.
k: In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.

w: “You give them something to eat.”
k: Give ye them to eat.

w: “How many loaves do you have? Go see.”
k: How many loaves have ye? go and see.

w: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
k: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

w: “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
k: That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.

w: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
k: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.

w: “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
k: Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:

w: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
k: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

w: because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, thus purifying all foods
k: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?

w: making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
k: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.

w: “Ephphatha!”
“Be opened!”
k: Ephphatha, Be opened.

w: “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written,
‘This people honors me with their lips,
but their heart is far from me.
k: Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

w: “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
k: Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.

w: then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
k: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;

w: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’
and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
k: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:

w: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”
k: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.

w: “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
k: Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.

w: “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,
k: Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;

w: But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban,
that is to say, given to God”;’
k: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.

w: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
k: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.

w: “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
k: For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

w: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
k: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

w: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
k: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

w: But they worship me in vain,
teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
k: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

w: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
k: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

w: This was from the Lord,
it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
k: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

w: “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.”
k: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.

w: But about the dead, that they are raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
k: And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?

w: “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.
k: A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.

w: Again he sent another; and they killed him; and many others, beating some, and killing some.
k: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.

w: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
k: And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.

w: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
k: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.

w: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
k: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.

w: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
k: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.

w: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
k: Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.

w: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
k: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.

w: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?”
k: David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son?

w: “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?
k: Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?

w: and the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts:
k: And the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts:

w: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’
This is the first commandment.
k: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.

w: “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:
k: The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:

w: “Whose is this image and inscription?”
k: Whose is this image and superscription?

w: “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
k: Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:

w: “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
k: Why tempt ye me? bring me a penny, that I may see

w: “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
k: Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.

w: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
k: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater damnation.

w: “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
k: How say the scribes that Christ is the Son of David?

w: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
k: And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.

w: Haven’t you even read this Scripture:
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.
k: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:

w: “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
k: Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces,

w: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
k: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.

w: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
k: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

w: The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
There is no other commandment greater than these.”
k: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.

w: For David himself said in the Holy Spirit,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
k: For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.
And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

w: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?”
k: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up?

w: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?”
k: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up?

w: “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet, neither understand? Is your heart still hardened?
k: Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?

w: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him, when he comes in his Father’s glory, with the holy angels.”
k: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

w: “Don’t enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”
k: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

w: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
k: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

w: “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
k: Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.

w: “How many loaves do you have?”
k: How many loaves have ye?

w: “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”
k: Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

w: “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
k: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

w: “But who do you say that I am?”
k: But whom say ye that I am?

w: If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”
k: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.

w: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.
k: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.

w: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
k: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

w: “Why does this generation
seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
k: Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

w: “Don’t you understand yet?”
k: How is it that ye do not understand?

w: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
k: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?

w: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.
k: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

w: “Who do men say that I am?”
k: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

w: “I want to. Be made clean.”
k: I will; be thou clean.

w: “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
k: Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

w: “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
k: Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

w: “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
k: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

w: “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
k: Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.

w: “See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
k: See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

w: “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?
k: Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour?

w: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
k: But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.

w: “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
k: It is one of the twelve, that dippeth with me in the dish.

w: “I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”
k: I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

w: “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
k: Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.

w: “Go into the city, and there you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water. Follow him,
k: Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.

w: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
k: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.

w: “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
k: Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

w: “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch.”
k: My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death: tarry ye here, and watch.

w: “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
k: Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me?

w: “Most certainly I tell you, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
k: Verily I say unto thee, That this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.

w: “Take, eat. This is my body.”
k: Take, eat: this is my body.

w: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
k: Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.

w: “Sit here, while I pray.”
k: Sit ye here, while I shall pray.

w: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
k: And wheresoever he shall go in, say ye to the goodman of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

w: Arise, let us be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
k: Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.

w: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
k: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.

w: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
k: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.

w: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
k: Verily I say unto you, I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, until that day that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.

w: “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”
k: Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.

w: “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
k: This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.

w: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.
k: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.

w: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
k: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

w: For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
k: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.

w: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
k: And he will shew you a large upper room furnished and prepared: there make ready for us.

w: “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
k: Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.

w: “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
k: All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.

w: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
k: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

w: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder, unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
k: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

w: Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;
k: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

w: “Stretch out your hand.”
k: Stretch forth thine hand.

w: “Stand up.”
k: Stand forth.

w: but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
k: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:

w: If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.
k: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

w: “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
k: Who is my mother, or my brethren?

w: For whoever does the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.”
k: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.

w: “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
k: Behold my mother and my brethren!

w: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
k: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

w: “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
k: Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill?

w: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
k: How can Satan cast out Satan?

w: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.
k: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

w: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
k: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

w: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’
k: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

w: “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
k: Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

w: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
k: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

w: “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
k: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

w: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”
k: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins,

w: “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
k: Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

w: “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
k: Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

w: “Follow me.”
k: Follow me.

w: “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
k: They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

w: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
k: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?

w: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
k: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

w: “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
k: Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.

w: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
k: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

w: “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?”
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
k: Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

w: “So you say.”
k: Thou sayest it.

w: “Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation.
k: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.

w: they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
k: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

w: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
k: And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues;

w: He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who disbelieves will be condemned.
k: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
